findings.title: Dead code: two ASN1Encoder instances created and immediately discarded
findings.body: In `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, lines 114-115 create two `ASN1Encoder` instances via `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)`, but their results are never used. The actual encoding is performed on lines 117-121. These lines are dead code that allocate objects unnecessarily and suggest a copy-paste error. They should be removed.

findings.title: New abstract method `order()` on public interface breaks external implementations
findings.body: The `order()` method is added to the `CryptoProvider` interface without a default implementation. Any external code that implements `CryptoProvider` (e.g., custom providers in downstream projects or the keycloak-client repository before it is synced) will fail to compile. Providing a default method (e.g., `default int order() { return 0; }`) would preserve backward compatibility while still allowing the ordering mechanism.

findings.title: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns the default KeyStore provider, not BouncyCastle
findings.body: The method `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is documented to return the BouncyCastle security provider, but this implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is typically the SUN or SunJSSE provider. If any code path in the authz-client (or future code) calls this method expecting an actual BouncyCastle provider instance (e.g., to pass to `getInstance` calls), it will get the wrong provider. While most operations in this class throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, this method silently returns a misleading value.

findings.title: `readSequence` silently returns empty list for indefinite-length encoding
findings.body: If `readLength()` returns -1 (indicating indefinite-length encoding per line 134), the `while (length > 0)` condition in `readSequence` is immediately false, and an empty list is returned without any error. While ECDSA DER signatures should not use indefinite-length encoding, this silent failure could mask malformed input. A check for `length == -1` with an appropriate exception would be safer.

findings.title: `CryptoIntegration.init()` called on every `AuthzClient.create()` invocation
findings.body: `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` is called unconditionally on every `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` invocation. While `init` is idempotent (it checks `cryptoProvider == null`), it still acquires the `lock` object's monitor on every call after the first due to the outer null check being non-synchronized. Consider caching a flag or documenting that this is intentional to avoid confusion about repeated initialization cost.
